title: ਅੱਜ ਆਖਾਂ ਵਾਰਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਅੱਜ ਆਖਾਂ ਵਾਰਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ, ਕਿੱਥੋਂ ਕਬਰਾਂ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਬੋਲ
why_important: This is the defining Punjabi poem of Partition and one of the most culturally recognized poems in the language. A heritage learner gains a key reference for Punjabi collective grief and a phrase still invoked whenever Punjab faces tragedy.
phrases_in_general_usage: ਅੱਜ ਆਖਾਂ ਵਾਰਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ; ਕਿੱਥੋਂ ਕਬਰਾਂ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਬੋਲ
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਅੱਜ ਆਖਾਂ ਵਾਰਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ, ਕਿੱਥੋਂ ਕਬਰਾਂ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਬੋਲ
ਤੇ ਅੱਜ ਕਿਤਾਬੇ ਇਸ਼ਕ ਦਾ, ਕੋਈ ਅਗਲਾ ਵਰਕਾ ਫੋਲ
ਇੱਕ ਰੋਈ ਸੀ ਧੀ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ, ਤੂੰ ਲਿਖ ਲਿਖ ਮਾਰੇ ਵੈਨ
ਅੱਜ ਲੱਖਾਂ ਧੀਆਂ ਰੋਂਦੀਆਂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਵਾਰਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ ਕਹਿਣ
romanization:
Ajj aakhaan Waris Shah noon, kitthon kabraan vichon bol
Te ajj kitaab-e-ishq da, koi agla varka phol
Ikk roee see dhee Punjab dee, toon likh likh maare vain
Ajj lakhhaan dheean rondiaan, tainoon Waris Shah noon kahin
cultural_summary: Amrita Pritam's nazm is the best-known Punjabi poetic response to the Partition of 1947, transforming Waris Shah, the bard of Heer, into a witness for Punjab's collective grief. It is central to the modern Punjabi canon because it fuses feminist lament, historical trauma, and civilizational memory in a language that became shared across borders. The poem is commonly invoked in discussions of Partition, communal violence, displacement, and any later tragedy in Punjab that reopens the memory of mass suffering.
key_phrases_in_usage:
ਅੱਜ ਆਖਾਂ ਵਾਰਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ — invoked when Punjab faces a new collective tragedy, as a shorthand for calling history itself to witness.
ਕਿੱਥੋਂ ਕਬਰਾਂ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਬੋਲ — used rhetorically to summon a moral voice from the past in times of crisis.
ਇੱਕ ਰੋਈ ਸੀ ਧੀ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ / ਅੱਜ ਲੱਖਾਂ ਧੀਆਂ ਰੋਂਦੀਆਂ — cited to frame women's suffering as the measure of social catastrophe, especially in Partition remembrance and feminist discourse.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on Amrita Pritam's 2005 death year, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065 in life-plus-60 jurisdictions.

title: ਕਾਗਜ਼ ਤੇ ਕੈਨਵਸ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਕਾਗਜ਼ ਤੇ ਕੈਨਵਸ ਦੇ ਵਿਚਕਾਰ ਮੈਂ ਆਪਣਾ ਦਿਲ ਰੱਖ ਦਿੱਤਾ
why_important: This later Amrita Pritam poem is central to understanding her mature voice, where love, memory, and artistic creation merge. A heritage learner gains vocabulary for modern Punjabi literary self-expression and the recurring metaphor of life becoming art.
first_lines_gurmukhi: ਕਾਗਜ਼ ਤੇ ਕੈਨਵਸ ਦੇ ਵਿਚਕਾਰ ਮੈਂ ਆਪਣਾ ਦਿਲ ਰੱਖ ਦਿੱਤਾ
romanization: Kaagaz te canvas de vichkaar main aapnaa dil rakh dittaa
cultural_summary: This poem is often read as a key statement of Amrita Pritam’s later poetic voice, where intimacy, memory, and artistic making become inseparable. In the Punjabi literary canon, it matters for showing how modern Punjabi poetry turned inward without losing emotional and cultural reach. It is commonly invoked in discussions of women’s self-expression, autobiographical poetics, and the idea that lived experience is transformed into art.
key_phrases_in_usage: ਕਾਗਜ਼ ਤੇ ਕੈਨਵਸ — used as a shorthand for turning emotion or life experience into artistic expression; often cited when discussing Amrita Pritam’s reflective, self-revealing style.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on Amrita Pritam’s 2005 death, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2066 in life-plus-60 jurisdictions.

title: ਰੂਹ ਦਾ ਰਿਸ਼ਤਾ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਇਹ ਰੂਹ ਦਾ ਰਿਸ਼ਤਾ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਕੋਈ ਨਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ
why_important: The poem is widely remembered for expressing love as a bond beyond social naming or possession. A heritage learner gains one of the most recognizable Punjabi idioms of spiritual intimacy in modern literary culture.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਇਹ ਰੂਹ ਦਾ ਰਿਸ਼ਤਾ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਕੋਈ ਨਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ
ਇਹ ਇਕ ਐਸਾ ਅਹਿਸਾਸ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਰੂਪ ਨਹੀਂ
romanization:
ih rooh da rishta hai, jis noo koi naan nahin
ih ik aisaa ahisaas hai, jis da koi roop nahin
cultural_summary: This lyric is remembered as one of Amrita Pritam's clearest formulations of love as an inward, spiritual bond that exceeds social labels, marriage, and possession. In modern Punjabi literary culture, it is often invoked in discussions of intimate subjectivity, women's emotional autonomy, and the language of love that resists conventional naming. The poem remains especially resonant in heritage learning, recitation culture, and conversations about relationships understood as soulful rather than merely social.
key_phrases_in_usage:
ਰੂਹ ਦਾ ਰਿਸ਼ਤਾ — used to describe a deep soul-connection beyond formal or socially recognized ties.
ਕੋਈ ਨਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ — invoked for relationships or feelings that are real but resist easy labeling.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on Amrita Pritam's 2005 death, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065 in life-plus-60 jurisdictions.

title: ਇੱਕ ਸੀ ਅਨੀਤਾ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਇੱਕ ਸੀ ਅਨੀਤਾ, ਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਉਸਦੀ ਚੁੱਪ ਸੀ
why_important: This poem is often read as a landmark of Amrita Pritam's feminist and autobiographical mode, centering a woman's interior life rather than social judgment. A heritage learner gains insight into modern Punjabi women's writing and how personal narrative became literary resistance.
first_lines_gurmukhi: ਇੱਕ ਸੀ ਅਨੀਤਾ, ਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਉਸਦੀ ਚੁੱਪ ਸੀ
romanization: ikk see Aneetaa, te ikk usdee chupp see
cultural_summary: This nazm is frequently cited as an important example of Amrita Pritam's inward, woman-centered modernism, where a female subject's silence and emotional interiority become the real narrative. In the Punjabi literary canon, it matters for shifting attention away from moral judgment and toward lived female consciousness, and it is often invoked in discussions of feminist reading, autobiographical voice, and post-Partition modern Punjabi poetry.
key_phrases_in_usage: ਇੱਕ ਸੀ ਅਨੀਤਾ — used as a shorthand reference to a woman whose inner life, silence, or unspoken suffering is being foregrounded in literary, feminist, or conversational contexts.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the stated expiry, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065.

title: ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ, ਅੱਜ ਮੇਰੇ ਕੋਲ ਬੈਠ
why_important: This lyric represents Amrita Pritam's intimate love voice and is remembered as part of the emotional world that made her widely beloved. A heritage learner gains a feel for modern Punjabi address, tenderness, and the literary use of the word preetam in love discourse.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ, ਅੱਜ ਮੇਰੇ ਕੋਲ ਬੈਠ
ਇੱਕ ਗੱਲ ਕਰੀਏ
romanization:
Preetam, ajj mere kol baith
ikk gall kariye
cultural_summary: This geet is remembered for Amrita Pritam’s intimate, conversational love voice, where tenderness is expressed through direct address rather than ornament alone. In the Punjabi literary canon it stands as part of the modern lyric turn that made romantic interiority, feminine feeling, and emotional candor central to post-Partition reading culture. It is often invoked when discussing Amrita Pritam’s love poetry, the language of longing in modern Punjabi, and the affectionate literary resonance of the word 'preetam.'
key_phrases_in_usage:
ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ — a literary and affectionate word for beloved, still used in poetry, songs, and elevated romantic address.
ਮੇਰੇ ਕੋਲ ਬੈਠ — used evocatively to suggest intimacy, emotional nearness, or a quiet invitation to speak heart-to-heart.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the provided estimate, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065.

title: ਸੁਨੇਹੜੇ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਕਿਸੇ ਨੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਸੁਨੇਹੜੇ ਲਿਖੇ ਸਨ
why_important: As the title poem of a major collection, it helped establish Amrita Pritam's reputation for turning longing and message-bearing into a modern idiom. A heritage learner gains a culturally important word, sunehṛe, that links poetry, letters, and emotional distance.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਕਿਸੇ ਨੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਸੁਨੇਹੜੇ ਲਿਖੇ ਸਨ
ਵਾਂਗੂਂ ਅੱਖਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਹੰਝੂ
ਵਾਂਗੂਂ ਕਾਗਜ਼ਾਂ ਦੇ ਬੁੱਲ੍ਹ
romanization:
kise ne mere vaaste sunehRe likhe san
vaangoon akhkharan de hanjhoo
vaangoon kaagzaan de bullh
cultural_summary: As the title poem of Amrita Pritam's 1955 collection, this lyric is often cited as a key example of how she modernized the older Punjabi idea of the message-bearing love poem by linking letters, absence, and intimate emotional speech. In the Punjabi literary canon it matters for its compressed, feminine, inward voice, and it is commonly invoked in discussions of viraha, epistolary longing, women's subjectivity, and post-Partition emotional distance.
key_phrases_in_usage:
ਸੁਨੇਹੜੇ — used to mean tender messages, love-notes, or emotionally charged remembrances, often with a literary or nostalgic tone.
ਅੱਖਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਹੰਝੂ — invoked for writing that feels tear-soaked or emotionally raw.
ਕਾਗਜ਼ਾਂ ਦੇ ਬੁੱਲ੍ਹ — used metaphorically for letters or pages that seem to speak with intimacy.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on Amrita Pritam's death in 2005, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065 in life-plus-60 jurisdictions.

title: ਕੋਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਣਦਾ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਕੋਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਕਿ ਦਿਲ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ
why_important: This poem is valued for its existential tone and its inward, reflective style that broadened Punjabi lyric beyond romance alone. A heritage learner gains exposure to Amrita's philosophical vocabulary and a common modern Punjabi way of speaking about unknowability.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਕੋਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਕਿ ਦਿਲ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ
ਕੋਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਣਦਾ
romanization:
Koi nahin jaanda ki dil kithe vassda hai
Koi nahin jaanda
cultural_summary: This poem is remembered for extending modern Punjabi lyric into an inward, existential register, where uncertainty itself becomes the subject rather than romance, nation, or social role alone. In Amrita Pritam’s canon, it represents her reflective philosophical voice and is often invoked in discussions of interiority, emotional unknowability, and the modern Punjabi idiom of speaking about what cannot be fully explained.
key_phrases_in_usage: ਕੋਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਣਦਾ — used in everyday speech and literary discussion to express radical uncertainty, emotional unknowability, or the limits of human understanding.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the stated expiry, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065.

title: ਮੇਰੀ ਕਵਿਤਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਮੇਰੀ ਕਵਿਤਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ ਦਾ ਹੋਰ ਨਾਂ ਹੈ
why_important: This meta-poetic poem is important because it states Amrita Pritam's lifelong idea that writing and living cannot be separated. A heritage learner gains a concise entry point into Punjabi literary self-consciousness and the prestige of poetry as lived experience.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਮੇਰੀ ਕਵਿਤਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ ਦਾ ਹੋਰ ਨਾਂ ਹੈ
ਜਦੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਜੀਉਂਦੀ ਹਾਂ
ਮੈਂ ਕਵਿਤਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਲਿਖਦੀ
ਕਵਿਤਾ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਲਿਖਦੀ ਹੈ
romanization:
Meri kavita meri zindagi da hor naa hai
Jadon main jeeundi haan
Main kavita nahin likhdi
Kavita mainu likhdi hai
cultural_summary: This poem is a compact statement of Amrita Pritam's enduring belief that poetry is not separate from lived experience but is the very form through which life becomes meaningful. In the Punjabi literary canon, it is often cited in discussions of poetic selfhood, women's authorship, and modern Punjabi literary consciousness, especially when reflecting on the writer's vocation and the intimate bond between art and life.
key_phrases_in_usage:
ਮੇਰੀ ਕਵਿਤਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ — quoted to describe a total identification between one's creative work and one's lived life.
ਕਵਿਤਾ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਲਿਖਦੀ ਹੈ — invoked to suggest that true art emerges from inner necessity rather than deliberate craft alone.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on Amrita Pritam's death in 2005, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065.

title: ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਵਾਟਾਂ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਵਾਟਾਂ ਨੇ ਤੇ ਪੈਰ ਅਜੇ ਵੀ ਤੁਰਦੇ ਨੇ
why_important: The poem's journey motif made it resonate with displacement, exile, and emotional distance in post-Partition Punjabi memory. A heritage learner gains a phrase that speaks both to migration history and to the long emotional roads of diaspora life.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਵਾਟਾਂ ਨੇ ਤੇ ਪੈਰ ਅਜੇ ਵੀ ਤੁਰਦੇ ਨੇ
ਇੱਕ ਦੂਰੋਂ ਆਵਾਜ਼ ਆਈ ਸੀ, ਅਜੇ ਵੀ ਸੁਣਦੇ ਨੇ
romanization:
Lammiaan vaataan ne te pair aje vee turde ne
Ikk dooron aawaaz aaee see, aje vee sunde ne
cultural_summary: This lyric is remembered for turning the image of a long road into a powerful post-Partition metaphor for separation, endurance, and unfinished emotional journeys. In Amrita Pritam's canon, it stands with her most resonant poems of loss and inward survival, and it is often invoked in discussions of migration, exile, women's memory, and Punjabi diaspora feeling.
key_phrases_in_usage: ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਵਾਟਾਂ — used to describe long journeys, prolonged separation, or the emotional distance of migration and waiting.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the stated expiry, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065.

title: ਅੱਜ ਮੈਂ ਸਾੜ ਦਿੱਤੇ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਅੱਜ ਮੈਂ ਸਾੜ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਨੇ ਚਿੱਠੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਰਿਸ਼ਤੇ
why_important: This poem is remembered for its dramatic image of burning letters, a modern symbol of emotional severance in Punjabi literary culture. A heritage learner gains a vivid example of how love, memory, and renunciation are expressed through everyday objects like letters.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਅੱਜ ਮੈਂ ਸਾੜ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਨੇ ਚਿੱਠੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਰਿਸ਼ਤੇ
ਚਿੱਠੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਰਿਸ਼ਤੇ
ਸਾੜ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਨੇ
romanization:
Ajj main saar ditte ne chitthian de saare rishte
Chitthian de saare rishte
Saar ditte ne
cultural_summary: This nazm is remembered for turning the ordinary act of burning letters into a powerful modern Punjabi image of emotional rupture, self-willed renunciation, and the afterlife of love in memory. In Amrita Pritam's canon, it stands as an example of intimate, interior lyricism shaped by post-Partition modern sensibility, and it is often invoked in discussions of heartbreak, women's voice, and the symbolic destruction of the past.
key_phrases_in_usage:
ਅੱਜ ਮੈਂ ਸਾੜ ਦਿੱਤੇ — quoted to signal a decisive emotional break or the symbolic ending of a relationship.
ਚਿੱਠੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਰਿਸ਼ਤੇ — used metaphorically for severing ties preserved through memory, correspondence, or old attachments.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the stated expiry, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2065.

title: ਬਿਰਹਾ ਤੂੰ ਸੁਲਤਾਨ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਬਿਰਹਾ ਤੂੰ ਸੁਲਤਾਨ
why_important: This is Shiv Kumar Batalvi's signature statement on longing and one of the most quoted lines in modern Punjabi literature. A heritage learner gains a phrase that functions as cultural shorthand for the sovereignty of separation, desire, and emotional pain.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਬਿਰਹਾ ਤੂੰ ਸੁਲਤਾਨ,
ਤੇਰੇ ਸਿਰ ਤਾਜ,
ਤੇਰੇ ਗਲ ਹਾਰ,
ਤੇਰੇ ਪੈਰ ਪਵਾਂ।
romanization:
Birhaa toon sultaan,
tere sir taaj,
tere gal haar,
tere pair pavaan.
cultural_summary: This lyric is one of Shiv Kumar Batalvi’s most iconic formulations of viraha, the South Asian poetics of longing, and it helped define the emotional intensity associated with modern Punjabi lyric poetry. In the Punjabi literary canon it is often cited as a signature statement of how separation, desire, and pain are elevated into a sovereign force rather than treated as mere private sorrow. The poem is commonly invoked in discussions of love, loss, Partition-shadowed emotional culture, and Batalvi’s image as the pre-eminent poet of yearning.
key_phrases_in_usage: ਬਿਰਹਾ ਤੂੰ ਸੁਲਤਾਨ — used as cultural shorthand for the rule of longing or the overpowering authority of separation and emotional pain.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the provided expiry, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2033.

title: ਮੈਂ ਤੇ ਮੇਰਾ ਵੇਹੜਾ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਮੈਂ ਤੇ ਮੇਰਾ ਵੇਹੜਾ ਦੋਵੇਂ ਇਕੱਲੇ ਪਏ ਹਾਂ
why_important: Known through the larger fame of Loona, this piece is anthologized for its intimate domestic imagery and emotional solitude. A heritage learner gains access to the symbolic Punjabi world of the vehṛa, where home space becomes a mirror of inner life.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਮੈਂ ਤੇ ਮੇਰਾ ਵੇਹੜਾ ਦੋਵੇਂ ਇਕੱਲੇ ਪਏ ਹਾਂ
ਨਾ ਦੁੱਖ ਆਪਣੇ ਨਾ ਸੁੱਖ ਆਪਣੇ
ਨਾ ਕੋਈ ਆਸ ਨਾ ਕੋਈ ਪਿਆਸ
ਬਸ ਇਕ ਹਉਕਾ ਹਉਕੇ ਵਰਗਾ
romanization:
main te mera vehra doveyn ikalle paye haan
naa dukh aapne naa sukh aapne
naa koi aas naa koi pyaas
bas ik haukaa hauke varga
cultural_summary: This nazm is valued in Punjabi literary culture for turning the everyday domestic space of the vehra (courtyard) into a powerful symbol of loneliness, memory, and inward desolation. Though overshadowed by the larger fame of Loona, it is often anthologized to show Shiv Kumar Batalvi's gift for making household imagery carry emotional and existential weight. It is commonly invoked in discussions of Punjabi home-worlds, intimate grief, and the emotional symbolism of rural and small-town domestic architecture.
key_phrases_in_usage:
ਮੇਰਾ ਵੇਹੜਾ — used evocatively for one's home-space, emotional interior, or remembered courtyard-world; 
ਇਕੱਲੇ ਪਏ ਹਾਂ — quoted or echoed to express abandonment, emotional isolation, or a house left desolate.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the poet's death in 1973, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2033 in life-plus-60 jurisdictions.

title: ਦਿਲ ਲੈ ਗਈਏਂ ਨੀ ਮਾਹੀਏ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਦਿਲ ਲੈ ਗਈਏਂ ਨੀ ਮਾਹੀਏ
why_important: This is among Batalvi's most performed love songs and helped carry literary Punjabi into popular singing culture. A heritage learner gains a classic example of how Punjabi romance uses direct address, musical repetition, and the beloved's theft of the heart.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਦਿਲ ਲੈ ਗਈਏਂ ਨੀ ਮਾਹੀਏ
ਦਿਲ ਲੈ ਗਈਏਂ ਨੀ ਮਾਹੀਏ
romanization:
dil lai gayeen ni maahiye
dil lai gayeen ni maahiye
cultural_summary: This geet is one of Shiv Kumar Batalvi’s best-known romantic lyrics and is central to his reputation for turning intimate longing into highly singable Punjabi verse. It matters in the Punjabi canon because it helped bridge literary poetry and performance culture, especially through mehfil singing, radio circulation, and later stage and folk-pop renditions. The poem is often invoked in discussions of Punjabi love lyric, musical repetition, and the emotional directness of address to the beloved.
key_phrases_in_usage:
ਦਿਲ ਲੈ ਗਈਏਂ — used to say someone has completely won one’s heart, often playfully or romantically.
ਨੀ ਮਾਹੀਏ — a classic vocative for the beloved, widely used in songs, performances, and affectionate cultural reference.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the stated expiry, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2033.

title: ਰਾਤ ਗਈ ਬਰਸਾਤ ਗਈ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਰਾਤ ਗਈ ਬਰਸਾਤ ਗਈ
why_important: This ghazal is remembered for its musical compression and for linking weather, time, and emotional aftermath in a memorable refrain. A heritage learner gains a phrase often used conversationally to suggest that an intense moment has passed, though its feeling lingers.

first_line_gurmukhi: ਚਾਰ ਹੰਝੂ ਡਿੱਗੇ ਤੇ ਇਕ ਨਵੀਂ ਕਵਿਤਾ ਜੰਮੀ
why_important: Often treated as a founding modern Punjabi lyric, this poem marks a shift toward inwardness, compression, and emotional modernity. A heritage learner gains historical perspective on how twentieth-century Punjabi poetry moved from older forms into a more personal voice.
first_lines_gurmukhi: ਚਾਰ ਹੰਝੂ ਡਿੱਗੇ ਤੇ ਇਕ ਨਵੀਂ ਕਵਿਤਾ ਜੰਮੀ
romanization: Chaar hanjhoo digge te ik naveen kavita jammee
cultural_summary: Prof. Mohan Singh's "Chaar Hanjhoo" is widely cited as an early landmark of modern Punjabi lyric poetry, signaling a move away from ornate, inherited forms toward inward feeling, brevity, and psychological immediacy. In literary discussion it is often invoked when tracing the emergence of twentieth-century Punjabi modernism, especially the shift to a more personal, self-aware poetic voice.
key_phrases_in_usage: ਚਾਰ ਹੰਝੂ — used as a shorthand for distilled sorrow, intimate lyric feeling, or the idea that deep emotion can generate art.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the stated expiry, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2038.

title: ਅਧਵਾਟੇ
first_line_gurmukhi: ਅਧਵਾਟੇ ਖਲੋਤਾ ਮੈਂ ਆਪਣੀ ਰਾਹ ਨੂੰ ਵੇਖਦਾ ਹਾਂ
why_important: This poem is remembered for its reflective midpoint image, making life's journey feel unfinished, uncertain, and self-aware. A heritage learner gains a useful Punjabi metaphor for being halfway through a path, whether in age, migration, or moral decision.
first_lines_gurmukhi:
ਅਧਵਾਟੇ ਖਲੋਤਾ ਮੈਂ ਆਪਣੀ ਰਾਹ ਨੂੰ ਵੇਖਦਾ ਹਾਂ
ਅਗਾਂਹ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਜਾਣਾ ਹੈ, ਪਿੱਛੇ ਕੀ ਛੱਡ ਆਇਆ ਹਾਂ
romanization:
Adhwaate khalotaa main aapni raah noo vekhdaa haan
Agaanah kithe jaanaa hai, pichhe kee chhadd aaiaa haan
cultural_summary: Prof. Mohan Singh’s “Adhwaate” is widely remembered for turning the image of standing midway on a path into a modern Punjabi meditation on self-examination, incompletion, and historical transition. In the Punjabi literary canon, it is often associated with post-Partition introspection and with the broader modernist mood of asking where one stands between past loss and future uncertainty. The poem is commonly invoked in discussions of middle age, migration, ethical hesitation, and moments when individuals or communities feel suspended between two directions.
key_phrases_in_usage: ਅਧਵਾਟੇ — used metaphorically for being halfway through a journey, life-stage, migration process, or difficult decision; it can imply incompletion, pause, or uncertainty.
copyright_note: This poem remains under copyright; based on the provided expiry, it is expected to enter the public domain around 2038.
